Diego —

Thanks for taking this early look. Our legal team is reviewing Redwood's standard US privacy addendum and we have a couple of open items specific to CPRA/CCPA compliance for healthcare-adjacent data:

- We need confirmation that Redwood will accept a "Service Provider" designation (not a controller) and will not "sell" personal information under any state law.
- Can you confirm what categories of subprocessors you rely on for inference (cloud infra, telemetry ingestion, monitoring/observability)? Midwest requires a named-list or a cadence for notice before onboarding new subprocessors.
- Data residency: we need options to pin processing to US-only regions; if not possible, what contractual safeguards (SCCs or equivalent) do you propose for cross-border support engineers or EU-based kernels?
- Deletion/retention: our policy requires deletion of inference logs within 45 days of request, and a separate backup retention maximum of 90 days. Is that feasible?

Attached: privacy_questionnaire_midwest.pdf (high level asks). Our outside counsel (copied separately) will propose redlines if needed. Looking for a quick sync — is this week possible?

Best,
Erin
Director, Privacy & Compliance
Midwest Health Systems

Erin —

Thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front and then proposed next steps:

- Service provider designation: we are comfortable taking the role of Service Provider (CPRA/CCPA service provider) for Midwest’s use case. We will not sell personal information and will process strictly on Midwest’s instructions.
- Subprocessors: primary categories are: (1) cloud compute (AWS), (2) managed monitoring/telemetry (Datadog), (3) analytics for usage/cost (internal Redwood billing stack). We typically provide a rolling subprocessor log and 30-day notice for changes. I attached a first-pass redline to illustrate the exact contractual language we prefer.
- Data residency: we can pin inference compute to US regions for this contract. For support/maintenance that may require EU/other regions, we can either limit access or rely on contractual safeguards; Marcus and Rachel, see note for legal options.
- Retention: our standard telemetry retention for production logs is 30 days; we can accommodate a 45-day deletion SLA for customer-requested purge of inference logs. Backups are trickier — we aim for 60–90 day lifecycle but can restrict backup retention for this account with an agreed exception in the addendum.

Next steps I propose:
1) Marcus — take the attached redline and prepare counter-language acceptable for Redwood (see section headings: definition of Service Provider, prohibition on sale, subprocessor notice, deletion timelines).
2) Rachel — can you pull SOC2 evidence and a mapping of subprocessor regions (us-east-1/us-central1) for Erin?
3) Erin/Jason — if Midwest has preferred redline, share it and we’ll respond within 3 business days.

Happy to set a 30-minute call. 

Diego
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Diego / team / Erin —

I reviewed the redline and flagged items that need careful wording. Key positions Redwood should hold:

1) Definition: Accept "Service Provider" language, but define it to explicitly forbid any secondary use or combining of personal information for Redwood’s own model training or product analytics. Phrase we prefer: "Service Provider means a party that processes Personal Information solely on behalf of the Business and does not retain, use, or disclose Personal Information for its own purposes beyond providing the contracted services."

2) Subprocessor notice: We will provide a maintained subprocessor list and 30 days' notice before onboarding new subprocessors. We will not treat this as an approval right for the customer, but we will offer a 15-day temp mitigation window if Midwest objects (e.g., ability to keep processing on US-only nodes until resolved).

3) Data transfers: For this engagement we can guarantee US-only compute. However, we cannot prohibit support engineers from accessing logs from other regions in exceptional troubleshooting scenarios unless we build a custom support process and additional audit logging. If Midwest requires absolute prohibition on any cross-border processing, we should specify a restricted support SLA and add an administrative fee.

4) Retention: We can accept 45-day deletion for inference logs. For backups, I propose an account-specific retention of 60 days (compromise between our recovery SLAs and their 90-day ask). We will note exceptions for DOJ/other lawful holds.

5) Audit evidence: We can provide SOC2 Type II report redacted and a one-page dataflow diagram for Midwest to review.

I’ll prepare the suggested contractual text and attach to this thread by end of day.

—Marcus
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Diego / Marcus / Rachel —

Attached is Midwest Health’s redline to Redwood’s addendum. Two items to highlight from our side:

- We prefer the term "Contractor" in the contract (historical preference for healthcare vendors) but will accept "Service Provider" only if Redwood explicitly disavows any commercial use of the data, including model improvement, benchmarking, or analytics unless explicitly contracted.
- Subprocessor approvals: Midwest requests an approval right for any new subprocessor that would process PHI-adjacent data or be located outside the continental US. If Redwood cannot grant approval, Midwest will require a 10-business-day notice and the right to suspend processing until a remediation plan is agreed.
- Deletion window: we are pushing for 60 days for inference logs and 120 days for backup exceptions; we understand this may be negotiable but want it captured as the ask.

Please review the attached redline (midwest_redline.docx). We are willing to be pragmatic but have to preserve patient privacy and regulator defensibility.

Regards,
Jason Cole
Counsel, LawFirm LLP

Thanks for the redline and the clear priorities. Quick response with a proposed compromise so we can keep the deal moving: 

1) Terminology: Redwood accepts the label "Service Provider" for this agreement and will add explicit language prohibiting model training, benchmarking, or any use of the customer’s Personal Information for our own product development absent an explicit, signed addendum.

2) Subprocessors: Redwood will provide the current subprocessor list within 48 hours and will give 30 days' notice for material changes. For subprocessors that would be located outside the continental US or that will process PHI-adjacent data, Redwood will provide a 10-business-day notice and a temporary US-only mitigation (location pinning) while parties discuss—unless the customer requires an approval right, in which case we’ll need to route to product/legal for a case-by-case evaluation.

3) Retention: Redwood agrees to a 45-day deletion SLA for inference logs and will commit to a 60-day maximum backup retention for Midwest. We will include standard lawful-hold carve-outs. If Midwest insists on 60/120, please flag and we’ll escalate.

4) Evidence & execution: Rachel will share SOC2 Type II and a dataflow diagram by EOD Wed. We can run a short call with Marcus to walk through the exact redlined text. If the redline is acceptable, we can execute via DocuSign (link below).
